adjudication_records.issue_text: `queued` datetime in `to_dict()` breaks JSON serialization through Celery, causing `apply_async` to raise TypeError and outbound sync tasks to fail to enqueue
`from_dict` cannot round-trip a JSON-serialized dict because `queued` arrives as a string, and the caught TypeError returns None, silently disabling cycle protection

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource.from_dict`, `cls(**input_dict)` will not raise `TypeError` just because `queued` is a string—dataclasses don't enforce runtime type checking. So a JSON-deserialized `{"queued": "...", ...}` would still construct an `AssignmentSource` (with `queued` as a string), not return `None`. Also, the cycle protection in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` only checks `sync_source.integration_id` and does not depend on `queued`, so it would not be “silently disabled” by the `queued` type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` default is evaluated once at import time instead of at instance creation, giving incorrect timestamps
`from_dict` swallows parse errors and returns None with no logging or metrics, making deserialization failures invisible in production

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`, `AssignmentSource.from_dict` catches `ValueError` and `TypeError` and returns `None` without any logging/metrics (`except (ValueError, TypeError): return None`). This makes malformed `assignment_source_dict` payloads silently drop the source context (as used in `sync_assignee_outbound`), reducing production observability. It’s not a correctness bug per se (callers handle `None`), but it is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/diagnostics concern introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: using `timezone.now()` as a dataclass default evaluates it once at import/class definition time, causing all instances to share the same timestamp; the fix is to use `default_factory=timezone.now`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: to_dict() returns a datetime that is not JSON-serializable, breaking Celery apply_async kwargs serialization for the assignee-outbound sync path

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` returns `asdict(self)`, which includes the `queued: datetime` field (default `timezone.now()`), i.e. a raw `datetime` object. That dict is passed into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs={... "assignment_source_dict": assignment_source.to_dict() ...})` in `sync_group_assignee_outbound`. If the Celery task serializer is JSON (common), a `datetime` in kwargs is not JSON-serializable and would cause enqueue/serialization failure. The diff alone doesn’t show what Celery serializer is configured to use, so the “breaking” part can’t be proven here, but the risk is directly introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: from_dict silently returns None on TypeError from string datetime, dropping assignment_source and re-enabling sync loops instead of failing loudly

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource.from_dict`, `cls(**input_dict)` will not raise a `TypeError` just because `queued` is a string—Python dataclasses do not enforce type hints at runtime. A string value for `queued` would be accepted and produce an `AssignmentSource` instance, so it would not “silently return None” in that case. The only `TypeError` paths visible in the diff are missing required fields (e.g., empty dict) or unexpected kwargs, which the code intentionally treats as `None`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sync_status_outbound accepts assignment_source parameter but no caller populates or checks it, leaving status sync loops unguarded (dead parameter)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_status_outbound(...)` gained an optional `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None` parameter, but the diff does not include any call sites for `sync_status_outbound`, so it’s not verifiable from this PR whether callers do or don’t populate it. The claim that this leaves “status sync loops unguarded” is also not supported by any status-sync logic changes shown here (the loop-prevention check added is in `should_sync(...)` and is exercised for assignee sync only in this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: sync_group_assignee_outbound enqueues one unbounded Celery task per linked external issue without batching (pre-existing fan-out)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `sync_group_assignee_outbound` iterating `external_issue_ids` and calling `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(...)` once per linked external issue (no batching/limit): `for external_issue_id in external_issue_ids: ... apply_async(...)`. This fan-out behavior is real and unbounded in the shown code path, but it appears to be pre-existing behavior (the change here mainly adds `assignment_source_dict` kwargs), so it’s more of a scalability/architecture concern than a newly introduced correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Task calls installation.sync_assignee_outbound with assignment_source kwarg that concrete integration implementations don't accept, causing TypeError and breaking all assignee sync

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `sync_assignee_outbound` task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)` (in `src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py`). However, in the shown mixin changes (`src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py`) the method signature update is done for `should_sync` and `sync_status_outbound`, but there is no corresponding signature change shown for the abstract `sync_assignee_outbound` method. If concrete integrations implement `sync_assignee_outbound` without `**kwargs`/`assignment_source`, this new kwarg could raise a `TypeError`, but the diff alone doesn’t prove existing implementations lack such a parameter.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssignmentSource.to_dict() leaves queued as a datetime object, which is not JSON-serializable for Celery's default JSON serializer, causing EncodeError and silent sync failure

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` the implementation is `return asdict(self)`, and the dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a `datetime`. The dict produced by `asdict()` will therefore include a raw `datetime` under `queued`. The diff shows this dict being passed directly into a Celery task via `apply_async(kwargs={..., "assignment_source_dict": assignment_source.to_dict() ...})` in `sync_group_assignee_outbound`, and then deserialized back with `AssignmentSource.from_dict()` in the task. If Celery is using a JSON serializer for task kwargs, a raw `datetime` is not JSON-serializable and would raise an encoding error before the task executes. This issue is directly introduced by the new `queued` field plus `to_dict()` behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: If pickle serializer is used, from_dict may receive a string-form datetime with no validation, producing AssignmentSource with queued as str instead of datetime

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AssignmentSource.from_dict` simply does `cls(**input_dict)` with no runtime type validation, so `queued` could indeed be a non-`datetime` value if present. However, the finding’s claim that this would happen specifically when a *pickle* serializer is used is not supported by the diff and is likely incorrect (pickle would typically preserve a `datetime`, not turn it into a string). The diff also does not show any actual path where `from_dict` receives a stringified datetime; the only consumption shown (`should_sync` cycle check) uses `integration_id` and ignores `queued`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: queued field default timezone.now() is evaluated once at module import time, so all instances without explicit queued share the process-start timestamp; should use field(default_factory=timezone.now)

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added dataclass `AssignmentSource` (src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py), the field is defined as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. In dataclasses, this expression is evaluated at class definition (module import) time, so all instances created without an explicit `queued` will share the same timestamp from process start. This is incorrect for a per-instance queued time; it should use `dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: from_dict doesn't validate field types, so a dict with wrong types (e.g., integration_id as string, queued as string) constructs an AssignmentSource with incorrect types silently

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource.from_dict`, the code does `return cls(**input_dict)` and only catches `ValueError`/`TypeError`. Python type hints aren’t enforced at runtime, so inputs like `{"integration_id": "123", "queued": "2024-01-01"}` will successfully construct an `AssignmentSource` with incorrect field types rather than returning `None`. This can break the new sync-cycle prevention logic in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` (`sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id`), since a string vs int would compare false and allow cycles.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cycle prevention via AssignmentSource only covers the assignee-inbound path; status sync, comment sync, and other inbound mutations can still trigger outbound sync loops

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds cycle-prevention logic in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` (blocks when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id`), but the only place that actually parses/threads this source through to `should_sync` is the assignee outbound task (`sync_assignee_outbound` passes `parsed_assignment_source` into `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", ...)`). Inbound assignee mutations now set `assignment_source` when calling `GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign`, which then flows to the outbound assignee task. By contrast, other sync paths (e.g., status/comments) are not shown being wired to pass an `AssignmentSource` into `should_sync`; `sync_status_outbound` is updated to accept `assignment_source` but there’s no corresponding propagation in this diff. The claim that other inbound mutations "can still trigger outbound loops" is plausible but not directly verifiable from this diff alone, so it’s more of an incompleteness/scope concern than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: IssueBasicIntegration.should_sync ignores sync_source entirely, so subclasses not using the new base revert to loop-prone behavior with no warning

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `IssueBasicIntegration.should_sync` now accepts `sync_source` but still just returns `False` unconditionally, so it can’t enable (or “revert to”) any loop-prone syncing behavior. The loop-prevention check using `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` is implemented in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync`, not in the base, and nothing in the diff demonstrates subclasses “reverting” to unsafe behavior due to the base ignoring `sync_source`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Task sync_assignee_outbound does bare ExternalIssue.objects.get and get_integration calls with no try/except, no retry policy or circuit breaker for DoesNotExist/fetch failures

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `ExternalIssue.objects.get(id=external_issue_id)` in `sync_assignee_outbound` without a surrounding try/except in the shown hunk, but the finding also asserts missing handling for `get_integration` fetch failures and lack of a retry/circuit-breaker policy—neither is verifiable from the provided diff context (the `get_integration` call isn’t shown, and task retry behavior may be defined by decorators/imports outside the shown lines). The claim overreaches what can be confirmed from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssignmentSource.queued dataclass field default `timezone.now()` is evaluated once at import time, so all instances share a frozen timestamp, and the weak test assertion (`is not None`) masks this bug

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` the dataclass field `queued` is defined as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` (new file `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`). That calls `timezone.now()` at class definition/import time, so every `AssignmentSource()` created without an explicit `queued` will share the same timestamp. The correct pattern is `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. The added test `test_to_dict` only asserts `queued` is not `None`, which would not catch this shared/frozen timestamp behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Core claim that other integrations should still propagate changes outward is untested — no test covers assignment from integration A propagating to linked issues on integration B

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new cycle-prevention logic in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(...)` that returns `False` only when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id`, with an explicit comment that this "should still allow other integrations to propagate changes outward." Tests added/modified cover (1) `assignment_source=None` still syncing outbound (`test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign`) and (2) matching source integration preventing outbound sync (`test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration`). There is no test exercising the new branch where `assignment_source` is provided but has a *different* `integration_id`, which is the behavior asserted by the comment/finding (propagation from integration A to integration B). This is a concrete, diff-grounded missing test for newly added nontrivial logic, not a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No integration test of the actual sync loop; only mocked unit tests, so the `sync_group_assignee_inbound` → assignment_source → celery task round trip is never exercised end-to-end

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `AssignmentSource` and propagates it through `sync_group_assignee_outbound` into the celery task via `assignment_source_dict` (serialized with `to_dict()` and parsed with `AssignmentSource.from_dict()`), and then uses it in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(...)` to prevent sync cycles. The added/updated tests (`tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py`) patch `ExampleIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound` and assert calls, but they only cover the `assignment_source=None` path (task called with `assignment_source=None`) and the cycle-prevention path where `assignment_source` matches the integration and outbound sync is skipped (so the celery task/round-trip serialization isn’t exercised). There is no end-to-end test in this diff that runs the inbound assignment source propagation through `sync_group_assignee_inbound` → `GroupAssignee.assign(...assignment_source=...)` → `sync_group_assignee_outbound(...assignment_source=...)` → celery task `sync_assignee_outbound` parsing `assignment_source_dict` and delivering it to the integration installation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `to_dict()` → `from_dict()` round trip is untested, and `from_dict` performs no validation/type coercion, so a string `queued` value would be accepted and cause misbehavior

adjudication.rationale: The new `AssignmentSource.from_dict()` simply does `cls(**input_dict)` and only catches `ValueError`/`TypeError` (no type checks), so payloads like `{"source_name":"x","integration_id":1,"queued":"2020-01-01"}` would produce an `AssignmentSource` with `queued` as a `str` without error. The added tests cover `to_dict()` and `from_dict()` separately but do not test a `to_dict() -> from_dict()` round-trip, nor do they cover `queued` parsing/validation. However, in this diff `queued` is not used anywhere downstream (only `integration_id` is checked in `should_sync`), so “cause misbehavior” isn’t directly verifiable from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `sync_status_outbound` abstract method signature changed to accept `assignment_source`, but no caller passes it, no implementation is updated, and no tests cover it

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature to accept `assignment_source`, but the claim that “no caller passes it” and “no implementation is updated” cannot be verified from this diff because no `sync_status_outbound` call sites or concrete integration implementations are shown here. The diff also doesn’t add any new status-sync logic that would require tests; it only adds an optional kwarg to an abstract method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `should_sync` guard logic has no direct unit tests for edge cases (sync_source=None, different integration_id, missing org_integration config) and the base-class signature change may break subclasses overriding the old signature

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new guard logic in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` to prevent sync cycles when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` and changes the base signature in `IssueBasicIntegration.should_sync` to accept the new optional parameter. New tests only explicitly cover the “matching integration id => no outbound sync” case (`test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration`) and only implicitly cover `sync_source=None` via existing outbound-sync tests; there are no direct tests for other edge branches like `org_integration is None` / missing config key (which now short-circuit to `False`). Also, changing the method signature can be a compatibility concern: any existing integration subclass overriding `should_sync(self, attribute)` (old signature) would raise `TypeError` when called with the new second argument (e.g., `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`), though the diff does not show whether such subclasses exist.

That would make the equality check (`"123" == 123`) false and bypass the intended cycle prevention. adjudication_records.issue_text: from_dict doesn't validate types, so a dict with correct keys but wrong types constructs AssignmentSource with silently corrupted fields

adjudication.rationale: `AssignmentSource.from_dict` simply does `return cls(**input_dict)` and only catches `ValueError`/`TypeError`. Python dataclasses do not enforce type annotations at runtime, so a dict with the right keys but wrong value types (e.g. `{"integration_id": "123", "source_name": 42}`) will construct an `AssignmentSource` without error. That can silently produce invalid `integration_id`/`source_name` types, which then affects downstream logic like `should_sync(..., sync_source)` comparing `sync_source.integration_id` to `self.org_integration.integration_id`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Status sync is not cycle-protected: assignment_source is only used for assignee sync; sync_status_outbound has a dead assignment_source parameter no caller passes, and status inbound/outbound paths never construct an AssignmentSource

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `AssignmentSource` and uses it to prevent sync-cycles via `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` (returns False when `sync_source.integration_id` matches `self.org_integration.integration_id`). That plumbing is only actually exercised for assignee sync: `sync_group_assignee_inbound()` constructs an `AssignmentSource` and `sync_group_assignee_outbound()` serializes it into the `sync_assignee_outbound` task, which then parses it and passes it into `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` and `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)`. For status sync, the diff only changes the abstract signature to accept `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None`, but no status sync caller/path in this diff constructs or passes an `AssignmentSource`, so the parameter is effectively unused here and cycle-protection for status is not implemented by these changes. This is a concrete incompleteness/consistency concern grounded in the diff, but not a directly verifiable new functional break by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: from_dict swallows all construction failures silently by returning None without logging, silently degrading to no source and re-enabling sync cycles

adjudication.rationale: `AssignmentSource.from_dict` catches `ValueError`/`TypeError` and returns `None` without any logging/metrics (new file `assignment_source.py`). Callers (e.g. `sync_assignee_outbound` in `tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py`) treat `None` as “no source”, and `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source=None)` will then *not* apply the anti-cycle check (`if sync_source and ...`). So if the dict is malformed/missing keys, the protection silently drops. This is a diff-grounded robustness/observability issue, but it only triggers on malformed input and isn’t a definite, always-on defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unnecessary serialization boundary in sync_group_assignee_outbound to task: passing assignment_source_dict couples the task signature to dataclass field names instead of passing the picklable typed object

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally introduces a dict boundary when enqueueing the Celery task (`sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs={..., "assignment_source_dict": assignment_source.to_dict() ...})`) and then reconstructs the typed object inside the task (`AssignmentSource.from_dict(...)`). The finding’s proposed alternative—passing a “picklable typed object” through the task signature—is not supported/justified by the diff and is generally incompatible with typical Celery JSON serialization. While the dict does mirror dataclass field names, that coupling is explicit and expected given the `to_dict()/from_dict()` helpers added in this PR, so calling it “unnecessary” isn’t verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test name/behavior mismatch: test_from_dict_empty_array tests an empty dict and duplicates test_from_dict_inalid_data; the actual failure mode (valid keys with invalid types) is never tested

adjudication.rationale: In tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py, `test_from_dict_empty_array` passes `{}` (an empty dict), not an “empty array”, and it asserts the same outcome (`None`) as `test_from_dict_inalid_data` (which passes unrelated keys). Neither test covers the distinct failure mode in `AssignmentSource.from_dict` where required keys exist but have invalid types (e.g., `integration_id` as a string or `queued` as a non-datetime), so the finding about a test name/behavior mismatch and a missing edge-case test is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssignmentSource.queued default is evaluated once at import time (dataclass field default timezone.now()), so all instances share the same process-start timestamp

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`, the dataclass field is defined as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. This calls `timezone.now()` at class definition/import time, so every `AssignmentSource()` created without an explicit `queued` will share the same timestamp for the life of the process. Dataclasses should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` for per-instance timestamps.

adjudication_records.issue_text: to_dict() output is not JSON-serializable: asdict() leaves datetime objects, causing Celery apply_async kwargs serialization failure for inbound assignee sync

adjudication.rationale: `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` returns `asdict(self)`, which includes the `queued: datetime` field unchanged (a `datetime` object). That dict is passed directly into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs={..., "assignment_source_dict": assignment_source.to_dict()})` in `sync_group_assignee_outbound`. If Celery/kombu is using a JSON serializer for task kwargs (common), a raw `datetime` is not JSON-serializable and can cause task enqueue/serialization failure. The diff adds this new path and no conversion (e.g., ISO string) is performed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: from_dict does no type validation, so a string queued round-trips silently without error

adjudication.rationale: `AssignmentSource.from_dict` simply does `return cls(**input_dict)` and only guards `ValueError`/`TypeError` (new file `assignment_source.py`). Python dataclasses do not enforce type hints at runtime, so if `queued` is present in `input_dict` as a string, construction will succeed and you’ll get an `AssignmentSource` with `queued` as a `str` rather than a `datetime`. However, in this diff `queued` is not used for any logic (only `integration_id` is checked in `should_sync`), so this is a robustness/validation concern rather than a currently verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: from_dict silently swallows ValueError/TypeError and returns None, causing should_sync to skip cycle protection entirely on malformed payloads

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AssignmentSource.from_dict` catches `ValueError`/`TypeError` and returns `None` (new file `assignment_source.py`). In `sync_assignee_outbound`, that `None` is then passed to `installation.should_sync(...)` (`sync_assignee_outbound.py`), and the new cycle-prevention check in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` only runs when `sync_source` is truthy (`issues.py`). So a malformed `assignment_source_dict` will effectively disable the new cycle-protection (fail-open). However, this is an edge-case robustness concern rather than a clearly verifiable defect, since the dict is normally produced internally via `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` in `sync_group_assignee_outbound` (`utils/sync.py`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cycle prevention only blocks echo back to the same integration_id; ping-pong loops between two integrations still occur with no hop counter or provenance

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s cycle prevention in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` only checks `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` and returns False in that case, i.e., it prevents sending an update back to the same integration that originated it. Nothing in the diff tracks multi-hop provenance or a hop counter when propagating (`AssignmentSource` contains only `source_name`, `integration_id`, `queued`), so a two-integration “ping-pong” loop is not prevented by this logic (it would still allow propagation to other integrations as the comment states). This is a real, diff-grounded limitation/edge-case rather than a demonstrably broken behavior in the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sync_status_outbound signature adds assignment_source but no caller passes it and no should_sync('outbound_status') check exists, leaving status sync unguarded (dead or incomplete API surface)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `assignment_source` parameter to the abstract `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_status_outbound(...)` signature (issues.py), but the only plumbing added in this PR is for assignee sync (`sync_group_assignee_outbound` -> task -> `installation.should_sync(..., parsed_assignment_source)` and `sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)`). There are no corresponding diff changes showing status-sync callers passing `assignment_source`, nor any new `should_sync("outbound_status", sync_source=...)`-style guard in the status path. This makes the new status `assignment_source` API surface look incomplete/unused in this PR (though not provably a runtime bug from the diff alone).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test patches sync_assignee_outbound mock rather than the guard's actual location, and there is no test proving a different integration's source is still allowed to propagate

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new guard logic in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` to prevent cycles only when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id`, with a comment that other integrations should still propagate. The new test only covers the blocked case (`test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration`) and does not add coverage for the complementary allowed case (different source integration ID should still sync). The claim that the test patches the “wrong location” is not clearly supported by the diff, since asserting whether `ExampleIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound` is called is a direct way to validate the guard behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Naming confusion: assignment_source parameter also covers deassignment/status semantics, which will cause drift when status sync is wired through

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AssignmentSource` is being used as a generic “origin of change” marker to prevent sync cycles (e.g., `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source=...)` and passing it through `GroupAssignee.assign/deassign` to outbound sync). Although the name `assignment_source` is also threaded into `deassign` and added to the `sync_status_outbound` signature, the diff does not show any incorrect behavior or any status-sync wiring that would “drift” because of this naming. The concern is largely speculative/naming-only, not a verifiable defect or concrete issue introduced by the change.
